title: CNC drilling machine hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Minimal conventional pressure-sequenced open-circuit hydraulic topology. A fixed-displacement pump draws from Tank.S and supplies a shared open-center 4/3 DCV plus a relief valve. MainDCV.A is the forward command branch: it supplies the clamp cap side through the dual pilot-operated check and also supplies the externally piloted forward sequence valve. The forward sequence valve opens only when clamp-side pressure is present at its X pilot, admitting flow to the drill cap side. Drill extension exhausts from the drill rod chamber through the one-way flow control in the metered A-to-B direction to MainDCV.B and tank. MainDCV.B is the reverse command branch: it supplies the drill rod chamber freely through the one-way flow control and also feeds the reverse sequence valve. The reverse sequence valve remains closed until drill retraction pressure rises, then opens to supply the clamp rod side through the load lock and release the clamp. MainDCV neutral is open-center, venting A and B work lines to tank so the clamp load-lock pilot pressure can decay and the checks can reseat.

evidence gap (automatic drill reversal at exact 100 mm stroke): The topology enforces clamp-before-drill and drill-before-release, but the brief does not unambiguously require a hydraulic end-of-stroke reversal mechanism.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power unit with relief protection
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S. Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and MainDCV.P. ReliefValve.T and MainDCV.T return directly to Tank.R. This realizes the open-circuit tank/pump/relief power unit and pressure-limited supply.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Pump pressure line relief to tank
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ReliefValve.P is connected directly to Pump.P and ReliefValve.T to Tank.R, so overpressure flow is diverted to the reservoir at the commissioned setting.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Single-DCV clamp-before-drill and drill-before-release pressure sequence
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: MainDCV extend supplies ClampCylinder.Cap through ClampLoadLock. ClampLoadLock provides low-leakage clamp holding with pilot release from the opposite commanded line. ForwardSequenceValve is piloted from the clamp supply/load-lock inlet so drill feed is admitted only after clamp pressure qualification. ReverseSequenceValve gates clamp rod supply until drill retraction pressure rises, preventing clamp release before drill return.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Pressure-qualified drill feed with rod-end meter-out and reverse-order interlock
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ForwardSequenceValve opens from MainDCV.A to DrillCylinder.Cap only after clamp pressure appears at its external pilot. DrillCylinder.Rod exhaust passes through DrillRodMeterOut in the controlled A-to-B direction during drill extension. MainDCV retract supplies the drill rod chamber freely through the one-way flow control, and ReverseSequenceValve keeps clamp release unavailable until drill retraction pressure rises.

design_decisions.decision: Use a fixed-displacement open-circuit pump supply with tank return and relief valve.
design_decisions.rationale: The brief prioritizes simplicity and provides no energy-efficiency or standby-unloading requirement. Open-circuit power unit evidence supports pump suction from tank, returns to tank, and relief flow to tank for overpressure protection.

design_decisions.decision: Use one shared open-center 4/3 DCV for clamp and drill sequencing.
design_decisions.rationale: A single shared DCV keeps the prerequisite clamp branch commanded while the sequenced drill branch opens hydraulically, avoiding independent electrical sequencing. Open center unloads the fixed pump and vents A/B pilot/work lines in neutral for load-lock reseating.

design_decisions.decision: Use an externally piloted forward sequence valve supplied from MainDCV.A and piloted from the clamp cap/load-lock inlet.
design_decisions.rationale: The drill feed branch must open based on clamp pressure, not common pump pressure or an electrical pressure switch. The external pilot from ClampLoadLock.A1 remains pump-supplied during the forward sequenced drilling phase.

design_decisions.decision: Use a separate reverse sequence valve in the clamp-release branch.
design_decisions.rationale: The forward sequence valve cannot enforce reverse order by itself. A reverse sequence valve fed from MainDCV.B gates clamp rod supply until drill retract pressure rises after the drill cylinder reaches its retracted end position.

design_decisions.decision: Install a dual pilot-operated check valve at the clamp actuator ports.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp must hold through drilling and drill return, and DCV leakage alone is not acceptable for a no-drift/static hold requirement. The dual pilot check locks both clamp chambers and releases hydraulically from the opposite commanded line.

design_decisions.decision: Use exactly one one-way flow control in the drill rod-end meter-out path.
design_decisions.rationale: The typed drilling workstroke requires adjustable non-compensated meter-out. During drill extension, DrillCylinder.Rod exhaust flows through DrillRodMeterOut from A to B; during retract, reverse flow from B to A is free through the integral check.

evidence_gaps.evidence_needed: If true contact verification is required beyond pressure qualification, specify a non-electrical contact/position method available in the catalog.

evidence_gaps.capability: automatic drill reversal at exact 100 mm stroke
evidence_gaps.reason: The topology enforces clamp-before-drill and drill-before-release, but the brief does not unambiguously require a hydraulic end-of-stroke reversal mechanism.

assumptions: Clamp advance is represented by ClampCylinder extension; clamp release is represented by ClampCylinder retraction.
Drilling feed is represented by DrillCylinder extension; drill return is represented by DrillCylinder retraction.
MainDCV actuation commands are outside the hydraulic topology; no electrical interface is emitted.
Relief, sequence, actuator area and pump-flow values are sizing and commissioning items, not additional topology components.
open_issues: Final relief setting near 8 bar, forward sequence setting near 3.3 bar, reverse sequence setting, actuator areas and pump flow are sizing/commissioning tasks.
Confirm whether pressure qualification alone is acceptable as clamp contact/force proof.
Confirm whether drill extension-to-retraction command is manual/controller-issued or requires an additional non-electrical end-of-stroke topology.
If the 3.3 bar clamp pressure qualification and 8 bar relief limit imply possible over-clamping, final clamp-force management must be verified during sizing and acceptance testing.

research_coverage.summary: Most core hydraulic principles are supported with real citations: open-circuit power/relief/return topology, clamp cylinder directional control with pilot-operated-check load holding, pressure-sequence clamp-before-drill logic, and drill-feed meter-out speed control at the rod-end exhaust. However, two critical drill-feed details remain insufficiently supported for an unambiguous safe topology: the selected/safe neutral behavior for the drill-feed actuator in the combined directional/sequence circuit, and the all-hydraulic automatic transition mechanism from controlled drill-feed extension to retract/return if that transition is required to be automatic rather than operator-commanded.

items.rationale: Findings provide cited guidance for reservoir-to-pump suction, pump pressure/supply line, manifold distribution, return to reservoir, and relief valve returning excess flow to tank above a preset pressure. The exact numeric relief setting is not sourced, but the topology and adjustable preset protection principle are supported; the designer can set the specified value using component data.

Findings support a double-acting clamp cylinder controlled by a 4-way directional valve, with neutral behavior selected so A/B work lines vent to tank when pilot-operated checks are used. The evidence also warns against blocked A/B neutral upstream of pilot checks because trapped pilot pressure can cause creep.

Findings provide cited load-holding guidance: pilot-operated check valves mounted close to the actuator, cross-piloted from the opposite work port, with A/B-to-tank neutral to let checks reseat. This directly supports preventing drift/uncontrolled clamp motion.

The evidence supports use of a double-acting drill/feed cylinder in a two-cylinder sequence circuit controlled by a 4-way directional valve, and supports extension/retraction flow paths generally. It does not sufficiently establish the selected safe neutral behavior for the drill-feed actuator in this combined circuit—e.g., whether A/B-to-tank float is acceptable, whether blocked ports are needed, or whether an additional load-control/holding element is required for a vertical or over-running drill feed.

The workstroke speed-control portion is well covered: meter-out throttling on rod-end exhaust during extension/feed, with a one-way flow-control valve/check bypass for free reverse/retract flow. The weak point is the requested 'automatic phase-transition pattern': the accumulated evidence supports automatic clamp-pressure-to-drill-start sequencing, but does not identify a cited all-hydraulic mechanism that automatically shifts the drill feed from controlled extension/workstroke to retract/return at the end of feed, if that transition is intended to be automatic rather than manual/operator-commanded.

Findings support a pressure-sequence circuit where clamp flow occurs first, a normally closed adjustable sequence valve blocks the drill/feed branch until clamp pressure rises, an external drain is required, and bypass checks support reverse flow. The cited two-cylinder example also supports the desired order cylinder 1 extend, cylinder 2 extend, cylinder 2 retract, cylinder 1 retract. The noted false-advance caveat is an important limitation but not a contradiction to a pressure-based interlock requirement.

Findings support leak-resistant clamp holding using pilot-operated check valves at the clamp actuator, cross-piloted for release and with vented work lines in neutral so checks close. The sequence-valve evidence supports keeping cylinder 1/clamp from retracting until after cylinder 2/drill retracts in a two-cylinder sequence. This is enough to design the clamp-held-while-drilling topology, subject to final integration details.

Findings support a normally closed adjustable pressure sequence valve that opens only after upstream/clamp pressure exceeds its setting, providing a hydraulic pressure-driven transition without an electrical pressure switch. The exact 3.3 bar value is a design setting rather than a separate topology claim, and the evidence supports adjustable set pressure behavior.

missing_or_weak_information: Exact missing claim for drill-feed directional control: a cited recommendation for the neutral-center condition and any required load-control element for the drill-feed cylinder in this combined sequence circuit, especially if the drill feed is vertical or over-running.

Exact missing claim for drill-feed motion profile: a cited all-hydraulic method for automatically transitioning from the controlled feed/extension stroke to the retract/return stroke, if the machine requirement truly demands automatic retraction rather than manual reversal of the directional valve.

issues.description: Evidence gap for true physical workpiece contact verification: Pressure sequencing proves pressure rise, but premature obstruction can also raise pressure; the brief accepts pressure qualification but contact-specific proof is not provided by this hydraulic pattern.

Evidence gap for automatic drill reversal at exact 100 mm stroke: The topology enforces clamp-before-drill and drill-before-release, but the brief does not unambiguously require a hydraulic end-of-stroke reversal mechanism.

design_issues.description: The clamp-to-drill transition is hydraulically pressure-qualified as requested, using the clamp supply/pilot line to open the forward sequence valve. This satisfies the specified non-electrical pressure sequence, but pressure rise alone does not independently prove true workpiece contact if the clamp is prematurely obstructed elsewhere. Treat this as a non-blocking limitation unless the requirement is tightened to require separate non-electrical contact verification.

The topology enforces clamp-before-drill and drill-retracted-before-clamp-release, but it does not add a hydraulic/mechanical end-of-stroke device to reverse the MainDCV after the 100 mm drilling stroke. This is acceptable if MainDCV reversal is an external command/operator action, but the requirement should be clarified if fully automatic non-electrical drill extension-to-retraction transition is required.

design_review.summary: The proposed topology is functionally valid for the stated catalog-level brief: open-circuit pump/tank/relief paths are present, one shared DCV commands the sequenced functions, forward pressure sequencing blocks drill feed until clamp pressure qualification, the clamp has pilot-check load holding with neutral pilot decay, the drill feed meter-out valve is correctly placed in the rod exhaust path, and a separate reverse sequence valve gates clamp release until drill retraction is complete. Only non-blocking clarification/evidence limits remain around pressure-only contact proof and whether drill reversal must be automatic.

The proposed topology is functionally valid for the stated catalog-level brief: open-circuit pump/tank/relief paths are present, one shared DCV commands the sequenced functions, forward pressure sequencing blocks drill feed until clamp pressure qualification, the clamp has pilot-check load holding with neutral pilot decay, the drill feed meter-out valve is correctly placed in the rod exhaust path, and a separate reverse sequence valve gates clamp release until drill retraction is complete. Only non-blocking clarification/evidence limits remain around pressure-only contact proof and whether drill reversal must be automatic.

policy.approach: Smallest proved design: clamp sized from the sequence-qualified pressure point, drill sized near the top of the envelope, and the pump governed by clamp advance.

actuator_decisions.justification: Forward drill admission is tied to the stated clamp-pressure transition; the clamp therefore has to make the required force at that condition, not merely at the relief setting. Tool sizing selects a 160 mm bore with a 90 mm rod.
The drilling workstroke is the drill load case; sizing near the ceiling leaves room for losses and relief clearance. Tool sizing selects an 80 mm bore with a 45 mm rod.

supply_decision.justification: Clamp advance is the largest unthrottled flow demand. Tool sizing gives a 25 cm3/rev pump delivering 33.75 L/min, a 0.55 kW motor rating at the pressure ceiling check, and NG6 directional valve capacity.

setting_decisions.basis: Set at the stated clamp-pressure transition; the selected clamp bore verifies that required clamp force exists by this pressure.
Set below relief and to be commissioned above free drill-retraction running pressure so clamp release occurs only after drill-retract pressure rise.
The evaluated setting proves the system pressure ceiling rather than landing exactly on it.

engineering_notes: evaluate_sizing_policy verdict: PROVED, with all six criteria proved.
Verified clamp advance velocity is 1.6785872904223338 m/min, and verified drilling feed velocity is 0.1060096963769553 m/min.
Verified drill-feed pump pressure is 7.776 bar with 33.2171371466446 L/min relief flow during the metered feed.
Oversizing index reported by the verifier is 2.533.
This is the preferred option because it is the smallest proved design and has the lowest installed power among the proved alternatives.
open_issues: Commission the reverse sequence valve against actual drill retract end-stop pressure.
Confirm that hydraulic pressure qualification is acceptable as workpiece-contact evidence.
